items.title: OpenAI の GPT-6 Astra で「歩ける5km四方の森」を作るなら
items.summary:
OpenAI の GPT-6 Astra で「歩ける5km四方の森」を作るなら
いきなり5kmは頼まず、100m四方から始める。海外で紹介された手順です😳
https://t.co/gPllReJX5d
Astra に100m四方の森を試作してもらう
↓
木の間隔、道、小川、岩、草の量を決めるルールを C++ で書く
↓
川底の石、倒木、シダ、池、ベンチを足す
↓
Unreal Engine の標準キャラクターで歩き、近くで見ておかしい所を直す
↓
100m四方に納得したら、同じルールで5km四方へ広げる
↓
光は Unreal Engine の標準機能に任せ、木登りなどの動きを足す
100m四方 → 5km四方で、面積は2,500倍。
小さな森が作り物っぽく見えるなら、広げても作り物っぽい森が2,500倍の広さになるだけ。
この順番は、ゲーム以外の制作にも使えそうです。
投稿で紹介された手順どおりに進めても、同じ結果になるとは限りません。

items.title: Falling snow, stolen kisses, and a love that never stands still.
items.summary:
Falling snow, stolen kisses, and a love that never stands still.

Created with GPT Image 2.6 + Seedance 2.5 on @openart_ai 

Prompt:

AUDIO RULE: Natural sound only. No music, no score, no voiceover, no dialogue. Ambient winter city sound and foley only.

MOTION RULE: Continuous movement in every shot. The couple never stop, freeze or hold a pose, and the camera is always moving. Every romantic moment happens while they walk, spin or run.

STYLE: Hand-painted illustrated look, matching the location reference: soft painterly brush texture, warm amber lamplight against cool lavender-gray snow haze. Same color grade in every shot.

CHARACTER LOCK: <<<image_1>>>  is a single character sheet showing two people. The TOP ROW is the woman and the BOTTOM ROW is the man. Match both exactly in every shot.
The woman (top row): messy curly dark-brown hair in a loose updo with loose strands, freckles, small gold hoop earrings. Long dark brown textured wool coat, white collared shirt, charcoal wide-leg trousers, black leather belt, black lace-up boots. She also wears a burgundy fringed wool scarf, as in the location image. She carries a paper cup of tea with the tea-bag tag hanging out.
The man (bottom row): tall, tousled wavy dark-brown hair, freckles. Long brown herringbone tweed coat, olive-green fringed scarf, cream cable-knit sweater, dark brown trousers, dark leather boots.
SCARF LOCK: His olive scarf stays on his neck and her burgundy scarf stays on hers in every shot. Scarves never move between people.
Faces, hair, outfits, heights and proportions never change between shots. They look at each other with deep affection and never look at the camera.

LOCATION: <<<image_2>>> , snowy Upper West Side at dusk. Gas-style street lamps, snow-covered trees, black iron fences, brownstones with warm lit windows and snowy stoops, a street sign reading "W 73 St / Broadway", a yellow taxi, the Empire State Building glowing in the haze. Soft snow falls throughout.

SHOT 1 (0:00-0:03)
Camera: Wide tracking shot gliding backward ahead of them down the snowy sidewalk, lamps streaking past.
Action: They walk toward us, his arm around her shoulders, her tea steaming. She leans her head against him while they walk, and he kisses the top of her head without breaking stride. Snow swirls through the lamplight and a yellow taxi slides by behind them.
Sound: Crunching, slushy footsteps, a muffled tire hiss, a soft contented sigh, gentle wind.

HARD CUT

SHOT 2 (0:03-0:06)
Camera: Medium shot, smooth handheld tracking sideways at walking pace, shallow depth of field.
Action: Still walking, he opens the front of his coat and pulls her in against his side, wrapping the coat around her shoulder. His olive scarf stays on his neck and her burgundy scarf stays on hers. She laughs, looks up at him, and catches a snowflake on her tongue. He grins and tucks a loose curl behind her ear as they keep moving.
Sound: Her bright laugh, wool rustling, quick footsteps, snow hush.

HARD CUT

SHOT 3 (0:06-0:09)
Camera: Low tracking shot at hip height, following their hands and the cup as they move, warm window lights streaming past.
Action: They swing their linked hands as they walk. She lifts the steaming cup to his lips and he sips, smiling at her. Snowflakes melt on his knuckles and her burgundy scarf fringe while the tea-bag tag sways.
Sound: Cup crinkle, a quiet sip, playful breath, soft footsteps, a car passing.

HARD CUT

SHOT 4 (0:09-0:12)
Camera: Fast but smooth circling orbit around them, snow flying through the foreground.
Action: He lifts her hand and spins her under his arm. Her coat flares and her curls swing as she twirls, laughing. She spins back into him and they keep moving in a flowing walking waltz down the sidewalk, foreheads close, eyes locked.
Sound: Coat swish, her delighted laugh, quick light footsteps in snow, a distant bell.

HARD CUT

SHOT 5 (0:12-0:15)
Camera: Sweeping crane move that begins close and rises into a wide pull-back, following them up the avenue with the Empire State Building glowing in the haze.
Action: Hand in hand, they run a few joyful steps through the falling snow, then he pulls her in and they kiss mid-stride, still moving, her scarf fringe flying. They keep walking away up the avenue, arms around each other, leaving two sets of footprints as the flakes thicken.
Sound: Quick crunching footsteps, a happy laugh, coat rustle, fading into the hush of falling snow.

AVOID: music, dialogue, text overlays, still poses, freeze frames, camera looks, face or hairstyle drift, swapping the two characters' outfits, scarves moving between people, any change to coats, scarves, earrings or boots between shots, photorealistic style.

items.title: Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon
items.summary:
Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon

they're made by a company called Stingray, and they already guard more than 50 million salmon and trout 24/7

the reason is sea lice, tiny parasites that latch onto salmon and feed on them

as few as 11 can kill a small fish, and one pen can hold 150,000 salmon

the usual fix is pumping the fish out and blasting them with warm water or water jets to knock the lice off

but the handling is so rough that Norway's fish health report ranks it the top cause of death in full-grown farmed salmon

so instead, Stingray puts a robot inside the pen that hunts lice one at a time, all day:

> two cameras watch every salmon that swims past

> AI checks two frames to make sure it's really a louse

> then a green laser fires from up to 2 meters away

> the salmon's scales reflect the beam, so the fish swims off fine and the louse is dead

we now live in a world where AI lasers do pest control on your dinner lmao

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. We’ll also make sustained investments in priorities residents help select.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
